cc:Work.dc:description: Each marker is the median of the 50 actual requests in its original chronological process block. The fixed role sequence is U,C,C,U,C,U,U,C, with U = upstream eager and C = compiled denoiser. The top panel uses a zero-based latency axis; the bottom panel shows each block median minus its own role's overall 200-request median, in milliseconds. The lower panel is a descriptive change of origin, not a speedup, noise bound or confidence interval. Block index denotes launch order, not elapsed wall-clock time. Four repeats of the same 50 scenes per role do not establish stationarity or cross-hardware generalization. Historical October 30, 2026 cohort: one NVIDIA H100 80 GB GPU and one fixed runtime. Each role has 200 measured requests from the same 50 scene groups, repeated four times; the 400 requests are not 400 independent scenes. Each request generates 24 future frames at 576 × 1024 with pretrained Vista and 50 denoising steps. Request latency includes input loading/preprocessing through host-ready frames and excludes initialization, compilation, warmups and output export. These figures describe performance and allocator memory only: held-out output-quality validation was not completed, and quality preservation is not established. No hardware cohorts are pooled.
